essay: Thrill Jockey is one of the rare labels whose genre is really a way of listening. Founded in Chicago in 1992 and operating as a 50/50 artist profit-share, it became a home for music that treated rock instrumentation as materials rather than rules: bass could behave like dub, guitars like percussion, a drum kit could imply minimalism, and electric jazz could still have the patience of an indie-rock band. This playlist follows the connective tissue around the label’s mid-1990s Chicago axis: Tortoise’s rhythmic engineering; The Sea and Cake’s airy songcraft; Gastr del Sol’s studio abstraction; the Chicago improvisers who turned post-rock into something jazz-shaped; and quieter guitar records that made space feel like an instrument. The through-line is not post-rock as a style but the willingness to let arrangements remain open long enough for musicians from different scenes to hear one another.
